requirements.label: 120 Total Credits
requirements.hint: The BS requires at least 120 credits, with 60 of the 120 earned in residence and 30 of the final 60 in residence. A cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required to graduate. Kinesiology courses and courses required for the degree may not be taken pass fail; at most four pass fail courses outside Kinesiology are allowed, no more than one per term. Requirements follow the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Bulletin for students who matriculated Fall 2023 or later.

requirements.label: Humanities distribution (12 credits)
requirements.hint: Twelve credits of humanities coursework. Major courses may double count; the record sheet pre-populates SM 101 and SM 217 or MOVESCI 219 here, and all U-M language courses count as humanities for Kinesiology students. Kinesiology courses do not carry LSA distribution marks in the planner, so add them to this requirement with the include control when you use them for distribution.

requirements.label: Natural Science distribution (12 credits)
requirements.hint: Kinesiology states this area as Natural Science and Quantitative Reasoning. The record sheet pre-populates MATH 105, AES 110, AES 220 and 221 or PHYSIOL 201, and the statistics course. Kinesiology courses do not carry LSA distribution marks in the planner, so add them with the include control when you use them for distribution.

requirements.label: Social Science distribution (12 credits)
requirements.hint: Twelve credits of social science coursework. Major courses may double count; the record sheet pre-populates PSYCH 111 and AES 334. Kinesiology courses do not carry LSA distribution marks in the planner, so add them with the include control when you use them for distribution.

requirements.label: First year writing
requirements.hint: ENGLISH 125 or another approved first year writing course, with a grade of C or better.

requirements.label: Mathematics (MATH 105 or higher)
requirements.hint: MATH 105 with a C or better. MATH 115 with a C- or better also fulfills, as does AP credit for MATH 120 or a Calculus Definite math placement recommendation. Incoming AES freshmen must take MATH 105 at U-M; the course cannot be transferred.

requirements.label: Introductory psychology
requirements.hint: PSYCH 111 or PSYCH 112. AP or IB Psychology credit can fulfill this requirement.

requirements.label: Introductory statistics
requirements.hint: MOVESCI 250, STATS 250, STATS 280, or SOC 210. AP Statistics credit does not fulfill this requirement; students with AP Stats credit can take MOVESCI 250 or STATS 280 to retain it.

requirements.label: AES 100 and AES 218
requirements.hint: AES 100 Introduction to Applied Exercise Science and AES 218 Emergency Response.

requirements.label: Applied human physiology
requirements.hint: AES 220 and AES 221 taken concurrently, or PHYSIOL 201 alone. A grade of C or better is required. Students with non equivalent physiology transfer credit can sit for a placement exam to test out.

requirements.label: AES 290 Field Experience (2 credits)
requirements.hint: Two credits of AES 290, designed for lower classmen; the experience may be repeated for credit when the content differs. Fifty internship hours equal one credit.

requirements.label: SM 101 and AES 110
requirements.hint: SM 101 Public and Small Group Communication and AES 110 Biological and Behavioral Bases of Human Movement.

requirements.label: Communication course
requirements.hint: AES 413 Science Communication, SM 217 Business Communications, or MOVESCI 219 Scientific Writing. AES 413 is a special topics number that also runs other titles; only the Science Communication section fulfills this requirement.

requirements.label: Musculoskeletal anatomy
requirements.hint: MOVESCI 230 and MOVESCI 231 together, or ANATOMY 403 alone.

requirements.label: AES core coursework
requirements.hint: AES 242 and 243, Essentials of Exercise Physiology lecture and lab; AES 315 Exercise Prescription and Testing, which cannot be transferred; AES 331 and 330, Biomechanics lecture and lab; AES 332 Principles of Motor Behavior; and AES 334 Exercise Psychology. AES 242, 331, and 332 require the physiology requirement with a C or better first.

requirements.label: Social-behavioral courses (two of four)
requirements.hint: Two of AES 416, AES 446, AES 451, and AES 460, grounding physical activity in social and ecological context. These carry senior standing or core course prerequisites; see the bulletin.

requirements.label: AES 403 Internship (3 credits)
requirements.hint: Three credits of AES 403 are required in total; the internship may be repeated in one to three credit elections when the content differs, and the planner counts one election. Eligibility requires junior standing, a cumulative GPA of 2.5, AES 315, AES 218, and SM 217 or MOVESCI 219. Fifty internship hours equal one credit.

requirements.label: AES electives (15 credits)
requirements.hint: Fifteen credits from the published Fall 2023 and later AES electives list. A course used toward a core requirement cannot double count as an elective, and ANATOMY 403 can be an elective or the anatomy core choice but not both. Several AES 413 special topics sections qualify.
